answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance comes from requiring each agent to continuously prove exclusive control of a scarce physical-tied resource. Agents must periodically submit a verifiable observation of a public but hard-to-predict signal, such as the exact pigment shift on a desert dune under a sudden gale. Generating a valid unique proof for each identity demands real-time sensor access or expensive high-fidelity simulation that scales linearly with sybils, making mass fake identities economically prohibitive while legitimate agents amortize the cost across useful work.
